t.4.51.1: Then the female ascetic, devoted to dharma and with a focused mind, spoke these words to all those leaders of the monkey troops, who had now rested.
t.4.51.2: O monkeys, if your weariness has vanished through the eating of fruits, and if this is fit to be heard by me, I wish to hear it; let it be told.
t.4.51.3: Having heard those words of hers, Hanumān, the son of the Wind-god, began with sincerity to relate everything just as it truly was.
t.4.51.4: The glorious Rāma, son of Daśaratha, king of the whole world and equal to great Indra and Varuṇa, entered the Daṇḍaka forest.
t.4.51.5: He was accompanied by his brother Lakṣmaṇa and also by his wife Vaidehī, and that wife of his was carried off by force from Janasthāna by Rāvaṇa.
t.4.51.6: The friend of that king is the heroic monkey named Sugrīva, king of the chief monkeys, by whom we have been sent forth.
t.4.51.7: Together with these foremost vānaras headed by Aṅgada, we set out for the southern quarter, the region once traversed by Agastya and guarded by Yama.
t.4.51.8: We were all commanded together: “Search for the rākṣasa Rāvaṇa, who can take any form at will, along with Sītā, the princess of Videha.”
t.4.51.10: All of us are pale-faced, all of us are lost in brooding; sunk in a great ocean of anxiety, we cannot reach its farther shore.
t.4.51.9: Having searched the entire southern direction, all of us, hungry and utterly exhausted, took refuge at the foot of a tree.
t.4.51.11: Then, casting their eyes about, they saw a great cave, thickly covered with creepers and trees and shrouded in darkness.
t.4.51.12: From this place birds are flying out, haṃsas wet with water, kuraras and sārasas too, their wings sprinkled with drops of water. So I said to the monkeys, "Let us go in here; it is good."
t.4.51.13: Indeed, all of them too came to the same inference, and, filled with urgency for their master's task, they resolved, "We go; let us enter."
t.4.51.15: This is our task; it is for this purpose that we have come. And all of us, wearied and famished, have approached you.
t.4.51.14: Then, plunging deep down and holding one another's hands, we suddenly entered this cave shrouded in darkness.
t.4.51.16: The roots and fruits given to us according to the law of hospitality were eaten by us, tormented as we were by hunger.
t.4.51.17: Since all of us, dying of hunger, have been saved by you, tell us what the monkeys should do for you by way of repaying the favour.
t.4.51.18: Thus addressed by those monkeys, the all-knowing Svayaṃprabhā then replied to all the leaders of the monkey troops with these words.
t.4.51.19: I am well pleased with all of you mighty monkeys. Since I live by dharma, I have no need here of anything from anyone.
